title: manager-first-90-and-career-mobility-playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes the recommended first-90-days onboarding for new people managers at Redwood Inference and the linked career mobility process for IC->Manager and Manager->Senior Manager transitions. It is meant for hiring managers, people ops partners, mentor buddies, and new managers. The goal is a predictable ramp that balances team impact, people development, and alignment to Redwood’s engineering and leadership expectations.

Who this applies to
-------------------
- New managers joining Redwood (both external hires and IC promotions).
- People managers who are new to managing at Redwood (including L3->L4 promotions).
- People Ops partners and Manager Enablement program leads.

Purpose and success metrics
---------------------------
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-impact for new managers while ensuring team stability and career development processes are followed.
- Success metrics (tracked by People Ops and Manager Enablement):
  - Manager cadence established within 30 days (weekly 1:1s with direct reports).
  - Performance calibration & development plans initiated within 60 days.
  - Manager ramp satisfaction >= 85% on 90-day pulse survey.
  - 90-day observational checklist completed and signed by manager’s lead and People Ops partner.

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary owner: People Ops (Manager Enablement subteam).
- Secondary owners: Hiring manager / Lead, Manager’s mentor/buddy, Eng Manager community.
- Escalation path: Manager Enablement -> Director of People Ops -> Chief People Officer.

First 7 days (Orientation and rapid context)
------------------------------------------
1) Before day 1 (Hiring manager):
   - Ensure equipment, accounts, and access are provisioned (IT ticket to slack-infra with priority tag).
   - Share first-week schedule and team org chart.
2) Day 1 checklist for manager:
   - HR: benefits enrollment briefing (link: /confluence/company-handbook/03_benefits-and-perks).
   - Tools: verify access to Redwood Console, Jira, GitHub org, PagerDuty, Confluence, and payroll.
   - Team intro: 30m all-hands + 1:1s scheduled for week 1-2.
   - Security: complete SSO onboarding and mandatory secure-sdlc training.
3) Deliverable by end of week 1: 1-page team health snapshot (current projects, open risks, people on team).

Weeks 2-4 (Stakeholder alignment and operational setup)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Objectives:
  - Establish 1:1 cadence with each direct report and upward 1:1 with your manager.
  - Meet cross-functional partners (SRE, Product, Design, Customer Success) to understand dependencies.
  - Review team backlog, current incidents, and recent retros.
- Practical steps:
  - Schedule weekly manager office hours for ad-hoc team coaching (30–60m).
  - Create or adopt team playing card in Confluence: responsibilities, oncall rota, code ownership.
  - Begin shadowing a weekly incident review meeting if team is oncall.

Days 30-60 (People & process)
----------------------------
- Objectives:
  - Begin development conversations (career aspirations, blockers) with each direct report and document in People Ops profile.
  - Baseline performance: review previous 12 months of 1:1 notes, PR review cadence, and any outstanding performance plans.
  - Operationalize team cadence: standups, triage, squad planning, and one-off working agreements.
- Deliverables:
  - Create 90-day manager plan (public to manager’s lead and People Ops).
  - Complete manager self-assessment and 60-day pulse.

Days 60-90 (Impact and calibration)
----------------------------------
- Objectives:
  - Lead an iteration planning and retrospective cycle end-to-end.
  - Work with People Ops to calibrate performance expectations for all directs.
  - Identify at least one mentorship pair and a cross-team collaboration to improve delivery.
- Deliverables:
  - Publish team performance dashboard (latency, error budget burn, cost per token estimates if infra owned).
  - Complete 90-day pulse and checklist; schedule a calibration meeting with manager’s manager and People Ops.

Manager checklist (quick reference)
----------------------------------
- Administrative: payroll setup, benefits enrollment, expense card, access reviews.
- Tools & infra: Console dashboards, team GitHub repo admin, PagerDuty rotation, SSO MFA.
- People: schedule recurring 1:1s, initiate onboarding plan for directs, set performance expectations.
- Compliance/security: complete secure-sdlc and data-handling training within 14 days.

Career mobility: IC -> Manager and Manager progression
--------------------------------------------------
- Promotion triggers (high level):
  - IC->Manager: demonstrated coaching, hiring involvement, cross-team influence, and ownership of hiring outcomes for at least 6 months.
  - Manager->Senior Manager: consistent leadership of managers, measurable team-level outcomes (throughput, quality, retention), and strategic contribution to org roadmap.
- Process steps (simplified):
  1) Nomination: manager or peer nominates candidate in Lattice/Promotion pipeline.
  2) Calibration packet: resume of contributions, 360 feedback, 3 example hires or coaching outcomes, and manager assessment.
  3) Promotion panel: HR + cross-functional senior managers review and vote.
  4) If approved: updated role description published, comp changes applied per compensation committee cadence.
- Timelines: typical cycle is 6-8 weeks from nomination to announcement for standard promotions.

Development resources and programs
--------------------------------
- Manager Enablement cohort: 6-week cohort with coaching, live case studies, and shadowing (owner: People Ops).
- Leadership book club: monthly sessions with scoped reading and applied practice.
- Engineering mentorship list: curated mentors for technical and people leadership.
- Recommended training modules (internal links):
  - Performance Management 101 (/confluence/company-handbook/people-ops/performance-management-101)
  - Salary & comp calibration guide (/confluence/finance-and-legal/compensation)

Hiring and ramping new ICs under a new manager
---------------------------------------------
- Before offer: agree on hiring rubric and scorecard with hiring manager and committee.
- First 30 days post-hire: manager should partner with recruiter and onboarding buddy to ensure technical bootcamp and OKRs are set.
- Interview debriefs: maintain consistent feedback using the standardized interview feedback form (link in recruiting templates).

Internal tools & templates (what to use and where to find them)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Confluence: manager playbook templates and team play cards (/confluence/company-handbook/templates).
- Lattice: 1:1 notes, performance reviews, goals tracking.
- Greenhouse: interview pipelines and scorecards.
- Slack channels: #eng-managers (community), #onboarding (logistics), #incident-review.
- Redwood Console: team cost and latency dashboards (request access through infra-oncall).

Example 90-day signoff table (to be filled and uploaded to Confluence)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
| Section | Owner | Status |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Administrative setup | Manager | Completed/Blocked |
| 1:1 cadence established | Manager | Completed/Blocked |
| Team health snapshot | Manager | Completed/Blocked |
| People development plans initiated | Manager + People Ops | Completed/Blocked |
| Performance calibration | Manager + Director | Completed/Blocked |

FAQ (common manager questions)
-----------------------------
Q: Who sets comp for a promoted IC->Manager?
A: Compensation is set by the compensation committee in consultation with People Ops and the hiring manager; expect 4–6 week lead time.

Q: Who signs off the 90-day manager checklist?
A: Manager, manager’s manager (director level) and the People Ops partner.

Q: Where do I find DEI hiring guidance?
A: Recruiting & DEI playbook in /confluence/people-ops/recruiting-dei-playbook.
